items.prompt: White has doubled pawns on the c-file (c2 and c3). Doubled pawns can come with compensation. Exactly one of these statements is true in the position. Which?

options: White has a pawn majority on the kingside.

claims.statement: White's doubled pawns: c2 and c3.
White's majority pawns: a3, c2, c3 and d4.

hints: Test each statement against the board; three are false.

Bishop pair: one light-squared and one dark-squared bishop. Majority: strictly more pawns than the opponent on the queenside (files a-d) or the kingside (files e-h). Passed: no enemy pawn ahead of it on its own or a neighbouring file. Protected: defended by a friendly pawn.
The true statement is about the bishops.
items.explain: True: White has the bishop pair. Bishop pair: white. White's majority pawns: a3, c2, c3 and d4. White's passed pawns: none. Whether the compensation is enough is not claimed here.
options: White has a pawn majority on the kingside.

items.prompt: White has doubled pawns on the e-file (e3 and e5). Doubled pawns can come with compensation. Exactly one of these statements is true in the position. Which?
